page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.34 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative weaknesses. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated in the bottom 25% at 3990.58, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is similarly weak at 26.13 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 36.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks and 311.23 GB/sec for cached small blocks. Conversely, write performance for large blocks is average at 25.99 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server achieves moderate throughput in static web serving at 7.74 GB/sec and small-model LLM inference, though performance drops significantly on medium-sized models.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the D4s_v6 is positioned as a cost-efficient general-purpose instance for workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or massive multi-threaded parallelization. It is well-suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and text processing tasks. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides qualitative hardware acceleration for small-scale machine learning inference, though the lack of a GPU and the weak multi-core scaling limit its suitability for heavy data science or compilation workloads.
